rules.note: RBI Indian Currency FAQ, updated 15 Apr 2025, opened 2026-11-01: one rupee consists of 100 paise. effectiveFrom is the FAQ revision date.
One thousand is 1,000 rupees. RBI defines 1 lakh as 100000, which is 100 thousands. The page was opened 2026-11-01.
RBI explanatory notes: Unit 1 lakh = 100000. Opened 2026-11-01.
RBI offers Rs. lakh and Rs. crore as reporting units. One crore is 100 lakh (1,00,00,000 rupees) in that system.
Indian digit grouping that goes with lakh (1,00,000) and crore (1,00,00,000): the last three digits, then groups of two.
Thousand, lakh and crore. RBI uses lakh and crore. Arab, kharab, nil and padma are not used.

UNVERIFIED as a cheque-words statute. At or above 100 crore the crore count is spelled in the same Indian system: One Hundred Crore, One Thousand Crore, One Lakh Crore, One Crore Crore. Arab is not used. Government English says lakh crore; the exact words line is a convention.
UNVERIFIED abbreviations. Short forms use a space: 1.2 L, 1.2 Cr, 1.2 L Cr, 1.2 Cr Cr. At most two decimal places, half-up, trailing zeros removed. Node Intl is not used.
